no extracutaneous involvement was observed
Multiple pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques on the left shin
Close-up examination revealed erosion with partially detached epidermis and multiple milia
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Histopathologic examination revealed several milia in the superficial dermis
Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant, c.6832G>T, p.Gly2278Trp, in COL7A1 (NM_000094)
Sanger sequencing confirmed cosegregation of this variant

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including progressive itchy erythematous papules and plaques, milia, and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the histopathologic examination revealing dermoepidermal separation and milia in the superficial dermis, are consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the COL7A1 gene, which is supported by the whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing results.

The patient's symptoms, including pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques on the left shin, are consistent with Lichenified Dermatitis, a dermatological condition characterized by chronic itching and scratching, which can lead to lichenification.

The patient's symptoms, including milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the histopathologic examination revealing dermoepidermal separation and milia in the superficial dermis, are also consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita, a rare autoimmune disorder that can cause blistering of the skin.
The patient's genetic testing results, including the novel heterozygous missense variant in the COL7A1 gene, support the diagnosis of a genodermatosis, a genetic disorder that affects the skin.
The patient's symptoms, including pruritic erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques, are consistent with Pruritic Dermatitis, a condition characterized by itchy skin.

The patient's symptoms, including milia, along with the histopathologic examination revealing milia in the superficial dermis, support the diagnosis of a milia-associated disorder, a condition characterized by the presence of small, white bumps on the skin.

rationales.F02: The presence of milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis is a characteristic feature of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa and Milia-associated Disorder.
rationales.F05: The presence of multiple pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques on the left shin is consistent with Lichenified Dermatitis and Pruritic Dermatitis.
rationales.F07: The histopathologic examination revealing dermoepidermal separation is a characteristic feature of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F09: The identification of a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 is a strong indicator of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F10: The confirmation of cosegregation of the variant by Sanger sequencing further supports the diagnosis of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
